stories.title: Government confirms UPI will remain free
stories.summary: The Finance Ministry stated that UPI will remain free for consumers and most merchant transactions. Any future Merchant Discount Rate charges would apply only to a limited set of transactions above a certain threshold. The amendment is intended to ensure the long-term sustainability of the platform.

stories.title: Indian Overseas Bank launches digital rupee app
stories.summary: Indian Overseas Bank has released a mobile application for India's Digital Rupee, supporting both person-to-person and merchant payments. The app includes UPI interoperability, allowing users to transact alongside existing payment applications. The bank says the platform is designed for security, ease of use and accessibility.

stories.title: NPCI defers UPI merchant fees
stories.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India has deferred the implementation of a 0.40 percent fee on select UPI transactions until after Diwali. Banks previously indicated that any gains from these fees would be reinvested into security and merchant expansion rather than added to their own profitability.

stories.title: Small finance banks lead on senior citizen deposits
stories.summary: Suryoday Small Finance Bank is offering an 8.6 percent interest rate on five-year fixed deposits for senior citizens. Large private and public sector lenders currently offer lower rates, ranging from 7.05 percent to 7.2 percent. Small finance banks continue to provide higher returns than their larger counterparts.

stories.title: Bank ordered to refund missing locker contents
stories.summary: The Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed Union Bank of India to refund ₹47 lakh after a customer discovered her locker was surrendered without her knowledge. The bank had continued to charge rent for the empty space. The refund includes interest and compensation for litigation expenses.

stories.title: Key dates for gold and silver investors
stories.summary: Investors in gold and silver are tracking three upcoming US economic releases in November. The schedule includes consumer inflation data, producer price figures and the minutes from the Federal Reserve policy meeting. These reports are closely monitored by markets for their influence on precious metal prices.

stories.title: Wedding insurance as a financial safeguard
stories.summary: Individuals can purchase wedding insurance to cover losses from unforeseen events like natural disasters or sudden cancellations. Policies are designed to protect the significant savings families often commit to large celebrations. The coverage addresses risks that remain beyond the control of the event planners.

stories.title: Tax rules for Diwali bonuses and gifts
stories.summary: Diwali gifts worth less than ₹15,000 annually are tax-free for employees, but cash bonuses are treated as salary income. These payments are subject to standard income tax rules. Salaried employees are advised to distinguish between the two when calculating their tax obligations for the year.

stories.title: NPS performance requires long-term perspective
stories.summary: Investors choosing National Pension System funds are warned that one-year returns can be misleading. Analysts suggest looking at consistency across market cycles rather than short-term performance. A fund's ability to limit losses during downturns is considered a more reliable indicator for long-term retirement planning.

stories.title: Government expands mandatory gold hallmarking
stories.summary: The government has added six districts to the mandatory gold hallmarking framework, bringing the total to 398 districts. The move requires jewellery sold in these areas to meet Bureau of Indian Standards certification. The latest amendment replaces the previous district-wise list to strengthen quality checks.

stories.title: Tax implications of job resignation payouts
stories.summary: Full and final settlement payouts, including leave encashment and bonuses, are subject to tax deductions. Employers typically withhold TDS on taxable components before crediting the net amount to the employee's bank account. Resigning employees are advised to account for these deductions when calculating their final take-home pay.

stories.title: Health insurance coverage for Diwali firecracker injuries
stories.summary: Comprehensive health insurance policies generally cover firecracker injuries requiring hospitalisation or daycare procedures. Minor injuries treated through outpatient consultations often remain uncovered, leaving policyholders to pay for certain treatments and consumables themselves. Accidents are occasionally excluded from the definition of a standard medical event.

stories.title: Managing your first Diwali bonus
stories.summary: Financial experts suggest using a first festival bonus to build savings and clear debt rather than spending the entire amount on shopping or gadgets. Because a bonus is additional income rather than a regular salary, it offers an opportunity to strengthen long term financial goals early.

stories.title: Correcting provident fund record errors online
stories.summary: Members can now use the online Member Portal to fix personal data errors like misspelt names or incorrect birth dates. The retirement fund body recently resolved a multi-lakh pile-up of grievances and introduced a WhatsApp channel for passbook access. The system is now attempting to be digital.

stories.title: Comparing Nifty 50 ETFs and index funds
stories.summary: Investors choosing between Nifty 50 ETFs and index mutual funds must weigh transaction methods, liquidity and expense ratios. While both products track the same benchmark, ETFs trade on exchanges like shares, whereas index funds are purchased directly from asset management companies. The goal is identical performance.
